extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and teams preparing Silver Anvil award submissions and press-release-driven campaigns
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and judging criteria for PR campaigns and press-release materials submitted to the PRSA Silver Anvil Awards, emphasizing strategic, measurable, and integrated media-relations work. Useful for PR teams preparing award entries or designing press releases that are part of larger campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations tactics (press releases, advisories, pitches, coverage requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics, programs and events driven entirely by media relations, including press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, and requests for coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries in the Media Relations category should demonstrate the effective use of media-relations tools (press releases, advisories, pitches, requests for coverage) as core tactics. Include examples of materials produced and how each tactic contributed to outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-page summary with measurable objectives and results (required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-page summary is required that clearly states measurable objectives and results for the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise one-page executive summary that lists objectives, the strategy that guided tactics, and quantified results. This is mandatory for Media Relations entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media impact documentation (media impact required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documented evidence of media impact is required for entries in the Media Relations category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply media-impression metrics, coverage lists, clips, and other measurable indicators of media reach and influence. Demonstrating multiple impressions and quality of coverage strengthens the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid promotions as complementary tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Paid tactics (sponsorships, paid placements, marketing communications) used to complement an overall PR strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how sponsorships or paid placements were targeted and strategic, served a distinct purpose, and complemented earned-media efforts rather than substituting for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid promotions: ROI and strategic targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Paid promotions should generate exceptional ROI and be targeted and strategic with a distinct purpose aligned to the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ROI figures, targeting rationale, and explain how paid elements were deployed to advance campaign objectives and measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated communications and creative integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative and effective integrated campaigns that combine paid, earned, shared and owned efforts with meaningful PR components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how PR work was integrated across channels (PESO model), coordinated with other disciplines, and contributed materially to campaign outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough research and benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of thorough research and benchmarking to inform strategy and tactical choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include audience insights, baseline benchmarks, research methods and how findings shaped objectives and tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, measurable objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns and releases must set clear objectives that are measurable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should be specific (e.g., awareness lift, impressions, behavior change) and accompanied by baseline and target metrics for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-based strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies should be demonstrably based on research and insights rather than intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect strategic choices to research findings and explain why chosen approaches were expected to achieve objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documented results and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must document results, showing evidence that objectives were met or progress toward them occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative and qualitative results (media metrics, behavior-change measures, partnership outcomes) and contextualize impact versus objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPIE — Research (benchmarks, audience insights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research stage of the RPIE framework: use benchmarks and audience insights to inform strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show what was measured before implementation and how insights informed planning and messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPIE — Planning (strategy, objectives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning stage: define strategy and objectives rooted in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline strategic approach, target audiences, objectives and the rationale linking research to planned tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPIE — Implementation (tactics including press releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation stage: execute tactics (including press releases) that align with strategy and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the tactics used, timing, channels, and how each tactic supported objectives; include examples of materials produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPIE — Evaluation (measurable outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation stage: measure outcomes against objectives using measurable indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show evaluation methods, metrics collected, interpretation of results, and any lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted to specific audience (strategic targeting; not mass blast)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications should be targeted to specific audiences rather than broadcasted as mass blasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate audience segmentation, targeting rationale, and distribution tactics (e.g., tailored lists, targeted placements) and note that scattershot mass distribution is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with broader campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases and tactics should be aligned with an overarching campaign strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the release fits into the larger campaign, complements other channels, and advances shared objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable media impact and multiple impressions documented
rubrics_metrics.description: Show measurable media impact and document multiple impressions across channels/placements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide impression counts, reach figures, circulation/airing details, and evidence of repeat or cumulative exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior change tracked / behavior-change evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Campaigns should track and, where applicable, demonstrate measurable behavior change among target audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include survey results, observed behavior metrics, participation rates, or other evidence that the campaign altered behavior; treat behavior-change evidence as high-value proof of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of partnership networks to amplify reach and impact (e.g., many partner organizations collaborating).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document partner roles, activation examples, and incremental reach or outcomes attributable to partner amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia and visual assets integrated
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of multimedia assets and prepared visual materials to support storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include photos, video, graphics, and other assets prepared for distribution; highlight how multimedia improved pickups, engagement, or messaging clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-channel coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordination across channels (earned, owned, paid, shared) to create a cohesive campaign presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show timelines, channel plans, and examples of coordinated activations that demonstrate synergy across channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthy hook and clear story angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should have a clear newsworthy hook and a defined story angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the hook succinctly; explain why reporters/audiences would find it newsworthy and how the angle was pitched or framed to media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotable spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of a compelling, quotable spokesperson to humanize the story and provide soundbites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of quotes used, their placement in releases, and how spokesperson media training or selection contributed to coverage quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual assets prepared (press-ready materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepared visual assets (images, infographics, b-roll) accompanying releases for media use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure assets are press-ready, available for download or distribution, and tailored to media needs to improve pickup and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality content over volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on high-quality, audience-relevant content rather than sheer volume of releases or distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how messaging, storytelling, and relevance drove coverage rather than relying on mass sends or quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of innovative or creative tactics that advance reach or engagement beyond standard practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe novel approaches, examples (e.g., creative demos, unique activations), and evidence those tactics improved outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of materials produced (supporting artifacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission should include concrete examples of materials produced (releases, advisories, pitches, multimedia assets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or reference sample materials that illustrate messaging, creative execution, and materials used by media or partners.
